info.title: LEDGER Reconciliation API
info.summary: Deterministic, auditable 1:1 transaction reconciliation over a versioned HTTP contract.
info.description:
LEDGER ingests independent Source A and Source B transaction records, preserves raw evidence, validates and normalizes into a canonical model, generates bounded candidates, applies deterministic matching, classifies seven reconciliation outcomes, records discrepancies, accepts authorized resolutions, and derives reports and exports from authoritative state.

## Versioning policy

* The published contract is **`/v1`**. It is the only version served.
* A request whose first path segment is a version-looking token other than `v1` (for example `/v2/reports`) is rejected with `404` and error code `unsupported_api_version`. It is never silently answered by `v1`.
* Backward-compatible changes may be made in place inside `/v1`: adding endpoints, adding optional request fields, adding response fields, adding members to open enum sets. Every such change updates this document's `info.version`.
* Breaking changes require a new `/v2` prefix: removing or renaming a field, changing a field's type or meaning, tightening validation, or changing the status code for an existing condition.
* Unversioned API paths (for example `/reports`) are accepted by the service boundary as a compatibility alias for `/v1`. **They are not part of this contract.** Integrations must call `/v1`.

## Authentication and authorization

Every operation except the `/v1/health` and `/v1/ready` probes requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A token is either an opaque token resolved by the configured verifier or an HMAC-signed token of the form `v1.<base64url-payload>.<base64url-signature>` when `LEDGER_TOKEN_SECRET` is configured. Principals carry roles and an optional `source_ids` scope. Reads are restricted to the caller's source scope; resolving a discrepancy additionally requires the `reconciliation_operator` role.

## Errors

Every error response has the shape `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "..."}, "correlation_id": "..."}`. `code` is machine-readable and stable; `message` is human-readable and not stable. The complete set of codes served by `/v1` is listed in `x-ledger-error-codes`.

## Correlation

Send `X-Correlation-ID` to correlate a request across logs; it is echoed in the response body. If it is absent the service generates one.

## Exports

`GET /v1/export` is a read-only projection. Raw payloads and sensitive-looking fields are redacted to `[REDACTED]`; exports are never authoritative state.

tags.name: Ingestion
tags.description: Source registration, batch creation, and raw record ingestion.

tags.name: Reporting
tags.description: Read-only derived projections over authoritative state.

get.description: Reports that the process is up. Exposes no business data and is exempt from TLS enforcement. Never requires authentication.
Reports whether the process can serve authoritative reads. Returns `503` with `data.status: degraded` when the database is unavailable. Exempt from TLS enforcement and never requires authentication.

503.description: The database is unavailable; the body is still the health data shape.

get.description: Returns reconciliation counts by outcome. `outcomes` counts every decision version; `current_outcomes` counts only current (non-superseded) versions. A caller scoped to specific sources may only filter by a batch belonging to those sources.
Returns the report, reconciliation rows, and discrepancy rows for the caller's scope, with raw payloads and sensitive-looking fields redacted to `[REDACTED]`. Read-only and never authoritative.

post.description: Registers or re-registers a source and the schema versions it may declare. Registration is idempotent for identical input.
Creates a batch for a source and schema version. A caller scoped to specific sources may only create batches for those sources. `(source_id, external_batch_id, schema_version)` is unique.

200.description: The created batch with zeroed counters.

post.description: Accepts one raw source record into a batch. Resubmitting identical content returns the original result with `duplicate_submission: true` instead of creating a new raw record, whether or not the idempotency key is reused; identical content targeted at a different batch links the same raw record to that batch. A syntactically valid but semantically invalid record is preserved as raw evidence and reported with `status: INVALID`.

200.description: The ingestion result. `duplicate_submission` distinguishes a resubmission from a first acceptance.

get.description: Returns the batch row plus its processing counters. A caller scoped to specific sources may only read batches belonging to those sources.

Lists every reconciliation version, including superseded versions preserved as historical evidence. Each row carries `outcome` (one of the seven reconciliation outcomes), `state`, `evidence`, and — for superseding versions — `supersedes_reconciliation_id`. Use `current_outcomes` from `GET /v1/reports` for the current view.

200.description: Reconciliation rows visible to the caller's scope.

get.description: Lists discrepancies raised by ambiguous or unresolved reconciliation decisions. `state` is `OPEN` until a resolution is applied.

200.description: Discrepancy rows visible to the caller's scope.

get.summary: Get the append-only audit trail for an entity
get.description: Returns audit events ordered by `sequence`. Audit history is append-only and never mutated. `metadata` is the structured form of the stored audit metadata.

200.description: Audit events for the entity (empty when none exist).

post.summary: Apply an authorized resolution to a discrepancy
post.description: Records an immutable resolution and transitions the discrepancy. The discrepancy must be `OPEN`. Requires the `reconciliation_operator` role. Resolving a reconciliation discrepancy creates a new superseding reconciliation version; the superseded version remains retrievable, and a repeated resolution request returns the already-recorded resolution and never overwrites history.

example.reason: Verified against the September bank statement.

200.description: The recorded resolution together with the updated discrepancy and resulting reconciliation version.

bearerAuth.description: Bearer token authenticated by the configured verifier. Signed tokens use `v1.<base64url-payload>.<base64url-HMAC-SHA256-signature>` and carry `subject`, `roles`, optional `source_ids`, and an expiry.

CorrelationId.name: X-Correlation-ID
CorrelationId.description: Client-supplied correlation identifier, echoed in the response body.

BatchIdQuery.name: batch_id
BatchIdQuery.description: Filter to one batch. The caller must be scoped to the batch's source.

EntityType.name: entity_type
EntityType.description: Audit entity type, for example `batch`, `record`, `reconciliation`, `discrepancy`, or `resolution`.

BadRequest.description: Malformed request: invalid JSON, a missing required field, an invalid field value, or a body exceeding the configured JSON depth limit.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated but not permitted: insufficient role, source outside caller scope, or a disallowed request origin.

NotFound.description: The endpoint, resource, or requested API version does not exist.

PayloadTooLarge.description: Request body exceeds the configured byte limit.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: A request body was sent without `Content-Type: application/json`.

InternalError.description: Unexpected server-side failure. The message is intentionally generic; use `correlation_id` to find the request in logs.

payload.description: Source-native record. Field names and required keys are defined by the batch's `schema_version`; the payload is preserved verbatim as raw evidence.

idempotency_key.description: Optional client key that makes a repeated submission of identical content return the original result.

OutcomeCounts.description: Counts keyed by reconciliation outcome. Absent outcomes are omitted rather than reported as zero.

evidence.description: Optional structured justification recorded immutably with the resolution.
